Prototype · legislative focus
OH! Civics game redesign

One game per module. More depth inside the game.

Instead of four small activities, each module now has one continuous experience. The complexity comes from the room, the people, the language of the bill, and the sequence of the process—not from dozens of cells, currencies, or dashboards.

Design rule

Stay in one governmental process long enough to understand it.

1Enter one richly illustrated civic setting.
2Meet people whose concerns change the bill.
3Watch the document and room evolve as the process moves.
Two modules · two deep games

Choose the process you want to inhabit.

Health stays entirely inside a legislative committee. Culture stays entirely inside bill drafting. Each playthrough has several acts, but they are acts of one game—not separate minigames.

Health · committee process

The Committee Room

Walk a fictional health bill through one committee hearing: briefing, testimony, amendment, member discussion, and a committee vote.

Only two persistent indicatorsCommittee support · Bill clarity
Culture · drafting process

The Drafting Desk

Turn a fictional arts-policy idea into a bill: hear the need, choose clauses, fit the bill together, survive a sponsor review, and print the draft.

Only two persistent indicatorsDraft clarity · Sponsor support
Ohio Lawmaking Lab

There is no four-game menu anymore.

This page is now the hallway between two deep rooms. Each room focuses on one legislative skill and lets the player experience several meaningful steps inside that skill.

1 game / module
OH!
OHIO LAWMAKING LABChoose one process and stay with it.
Why this structure?The learning target is no longer “manage the whole legislature.” The Health module teaches what happens inside committee work; the Culture module teaches how a policy idea becomes clearer legislative language. The procedural depth remains, while the number of simultaneous systems is kept low.
One continuous game · committee only

The Committee Room

A fictional health bill enters one Ohio-style standing committee. You will stay in this room from the clerk’s briefing through testimony, amendment language, member discussion, and the final committee vote.

Depth without overload

The room changes. The dashboard does not grow.

You will always see only committee support and bill clarity. Everything else is communicated through people, dialogue, marked-up bill language, and what physically changes in the committee room.

Process focusThis game intentionally stops at committee action. It does not ask the player to manage the House floor, Senate, governor, healthcare system, or state budget at the same time.
One continuous game · drafting only

The Drafting Desk

A fictional culture-policy idea lands on your desk. Stay with the same proposal as you hear community needs, choose clause language, assemble an irregular bill puzzle, respond to a sponsor’s markup, and print the finished draft.

Depth without clutter

The bill itself is the game board.

There are no sprawling maps or resource economies. The visual depth comes from a working legislative desk: folders, voices, puzzle-shaped clauses, handwritten notes, redlines, and the final printed bill.

Current representation matters: the U.S. House layer uses Ohio's 2022–2027 congressional districts because those are the districts represented by the current members of Congress through Jan. 2, 2027. Ohio House and Senate use the current 2024–2032 state legislative districts.

What about the new congressional map?
Ohio adopted different congressional lines for the 2026 election cycle. Those lines choose the representatives who take office in January 2027; they are not used here to label today's incumbents.

Research & source center

Every live question should store a source, date, status and expiration rule. Primary Ohio sources are preferred; high-quality state reporting adds context.

OH! Civics research snapshot is current through Aug. 24, 2026. A production site should refresh time-sensitive items automatically and retire or relabel items when legislative status or implementation changes.
